1) The product was already struggling because the yield was too low. There has been too much compression between its current yield and the risk-free rate with USTs rising since March. I have spoken about this all month.

2) Every time Bitcoin has a significant drawdown the product trades down from par. We have seen this on multiple occasions previously.

3) The reduction of the USD reserve to repurchase the converts may have caused some people to sell. Likewise the sale of 32 Bitcoin may have spooked others.

From March 2020, I was working as a home health therapist through the worst of the pandemic. In and out of people's homes. In nursing homes and skilled nursing facilities where half the residents were sick.

I was one of the few people most of these patients saw for months on end. Many of them were banned from seeing their own families.

I vividly remember one elderly lady. Sitting in her wheelchair, in front of a glass window, her family on the other side. Unable to stand or hear what they were saying. Tears rolling down her face as she reaches out and touches the glass. She can't understand why she's living like a prisoner. This woman, in the final days of her life, was forbidden from embracing her own daughter.. just inches away.

A weight comes over me. I've never felt so helpless.
That was just one of many heartbreaking scenes I witnessed over two years.

And my reward? Termination, without pay. Over a company-wide call.

And I wasn't the only one. Nurses sleeping on cots in those facilities, away from their families so they could keep serving patients.. Who were handed the same ultimatum: get the shot, or lose your job.

A few days after the call, we were told we could apply for a religious exemption, with no guarantee it would be accepted.

While scrambling to get ours approved, my wife and I had decisions to make. Even if we got approved, who's to say the system wouldn't pull another stunt a few months later and leave us jobless?

That's when I decided: I would do everything in my power to take control of my income.

Fast forward to December 26, 2021. My wife and I signed the closing documents on our home, jumped into a U-Haul, and moved to Florida… into my parents' house.

We made a good chunk of change on the sale, which gave me space in my life.

Over the next two and a half months, I spent my days journaling, praying, meditating, taking long walks, sitting still, digging deep to find out who I was, and asking God to pave the way.

At the end of those two and a half months, God revealed a direction.

It was time to start a business.

So I took some of the cash from the house and hired a business coach

I also took a job at a local PT clinic. Florida's regulations were far less strict.

One week into the new job, I took a week off and spent it in Tampa, building out the foundation of my coaching business.

This was the birth of Barefoot Will.

Fast forward to now.

In the first day of June, I made more money than I used to make in an entire month as a home health therapist.

My wife is a stay-at-home mom.

And I have complete control over my income.

No boss to answer to. 
No government agency threatening my livelihood.

Was it easy? No. Quite the opposite.

At one point I was working three jobs, living in a camper with my wife and baby, barely making ends meet.

I'll share more of the journey another time. The three jobs, the camper, the nights I wasn't sure we'd make it.

But here's what I know now.

Losing that job felt like the end of everything. It was actually the beginning.

If they'd never forced my hand, I'd probably still be trading my time for a paycheck. One company-wide call away from losing it all over again.

So if you're standing where I stood… scared, frustrated, lost.. hear me out:

The thing that breaks you can be the same thing that sets you free. You are not as trapped as the system wants you to believe. Trust God no matter the situation, because he has a plan!

Let that sit. The cost gap isn't double. It isn't ten times. It's roughly six hundred times cheaper to fake it than to film it.

Now the output side, which is where it gets genuinely absurd.

A human creator posts maybe three to five videos a week if they're grinding. The AI roster I analyzed was pushing out an estimated 19 videos per day across its accounts. That's not a typo. Nineteen. Every single day. Weekends included. No burnout, no sick days, no "I'm not feeling the lighting today."

That's roughly 570 videos a month versus a human's ~20.

Here's the math that actually matters, the part nobody talks about.

These accounts run on affiliate commission. TikTok Shop pays out somewhere between 5% and 20% per sale depending on the brand. Call it a $30 product at a 15% commission. That's $4.50 per bottle to the operator.

One of the videos in the feed I tracked had 512,000 views. The brutal truth of TikTok Shop is that conversion on a viral product video sits around 0.5% to 1% of viewers who tap through and buy. Take the low end. 0.5% of 512K is 2,560 sales. From one video. That's roughly $11,500 in commission. From one fake girl. From one clip. That cost about four cents of compute to generate.

And remember, that was one video out of an estimated 570 a month.

Even if 95% of their videos flop and get a few thousand views each, the portfolio approach means they only need a handful of breakout hits to clear five figures monthly. The model is built on volume the same way a slot machine floor is. They don't need every pull to win. They need enough pulls that winning becomes statistically inevitable.

I did a rough back-of-napkin estimate on the operation I looked at. Conservative assumptions, low conversion, only counting the videos I could actually find. The range landed somewhere between $40,000 and $90,000 a month in affiliate revenue.

Running cost: a laptop and a $23 API subscription.

Three new things I learned since the last post that I can't stop thinking about:

The "diversity casting" I mentioned last time isn't an aesthetic choice, it's an optimization. Each synthetic creator is essentially an A/B test. The operator watches which fake girl converts best in which market, then generates more variations of that winner. The feed is evolving in real time, like a marketing organism breeding toward whatever sells.

The brands often don't know. A chunk of these operators are pure affiliates riding a product the brand never authorized for AI promotion. The brand sees sales going up and a flood of "creator content" and assumes organic momentum. They're celebrating a trend that's actually a machine.

The detection window is closing fast. Six months ago you could spot these by the hands. The batch I looked at last week had clean hands, correct labels, accurate mirror reflections. The tells are disappearing one model release at a time. Pretty soon the only signal left will be that the person was simply never real and there's no way to verify it.

The takeaway hasn't changed, it's just gotten heavier. The single most valuable currency on the internet — a real human saying "I tried this and I liked it" — is being counterfeited at industrial scale, for the price of a streaming subscription, by people you'll never see.

Save this one too. And the next time a product is suddenly everywhere on your feed, ask yourself one question before you buy: who's actually telling me this, and can I prove they exist?

I'm working on a follow-up showing how to spot the last remaining tells before they vanish completely. That one might be the most useful thing I publish all year.

One of the best things I've learned throughout my trading journey is to combine these 2 manipulation phases together.

Both work on their own. But used together, they become the cleanest way to read this market.

Let me break them down properly.

The First Phase: Sentimental Manipulation

This is where price completely changes the bias and the direction retail is aiming for. Their target gets flipped against your bias.

It usually shows up in 2 ways:
A close below an S&R zone. 
Or breaking a key structure.

Examples:

Closing below support → retail sentiment turns bearish. 
Breaking a bullish structure low and shifting it bearish → retail sentiment turns bearish.

The whole goal of this phase is to flip the crowd's expectation.

But this alone is not enough to base a trade on.

Not every time retail sentiment changes does price actually flip.
That's where the combo comes in.

The Second Phase: Manipulation from Retail POI

The moment price flips retail sentiment, we wait for retail's trigger to actually take place.

So the full sequence becomes:

Step 1 → Sentiment Change. 
Closing below retail POIs or breaking structure.

Step 2 → Retail taking their position.

Now where exactly do they take action?

The moment price returns to their POI.

Example: We broke a support. Price returns back to retest it. That's exactly where retail steps into sells, just like every retail pattern teaches them.

That's the Manipulation from Retail POI in action.

Putting It Together
The moment price gives retail their dip back and offers them the chance to join the game.

That's when we frame their full position. Entry. TP. SL. And go exactly against them.

Always wait for both phases to happen. Never just one.
